item.title: Decode: RIP-Relative LEA
item.description:
Format: decode one instruction. Target: Windows x86-64.
Decode this byte sequence into its full assembly instruction (mnemonic + operands):
48 8D 05 12 34 00 00
Break down each piece: the REX prefix, the opcode, and the ModRM byte (mod, reg, rm fields). Pay special attention to what rm=101 means when mod=00 -- it isn't a normal register or [reg] memory form.
---
Answer: lea rax, [rip + 0x3412]
1. 48 is REX.W (W=1), so operands are 64-bit. 8D is the LEA opcode (load effective address, no memory access, just computes it). 2. 05 is the ModRM byte: mod=00, reg=000 (destination = rax), rm=101. 3. On x86-64, mod=00 with rm=101 is reserved for RIP-relative addressing (not a 32-bit-mode absolute [disp32]). The following 4 bytes (12 34 00 00, little-endian) are a signed disp32 added to the address of the next instruction, giving [rip + 0x3412].
